quizName: DMV Practice Test #5 20 Questions • Passing Score 16

questions.question: Which surface gives a motorcycle the best grip?

options.text: A gravel road
Dry pavement
Mud
Lane markings

questions.correctAnswerText: Dry pavement
questions.explanation: Dry pavement provides the best grip. Wet pavement, gravel, sand, mud, snow, ice, painted lane markings, and metal covers are all slippery and dangerous for motorcycles.

questions.question: To reduce your reaction time when a hazard appears, you should:

options.text: Always ride under the speed limit.
Keep your fingers on the clutch and brake levers.
Shift into neutral when slowing down.
Pull the clutch when turning.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep your fingers on the clutch and brake levers.
questions.explanation: In high-risk areas like school zones and construction zones, keep your fingers ready on the clutch and brake levers. This reduces the time you need to react to hazards.

questions.question: When carrying a passenger in a sidecar, you should:

options.text: Start slowing down sooner than usual.
Start slowing down later than usual.
Brake harder than usual to stop quickly.
Brake gently than usual to protect the brakes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Start slowing down sooner than usual.
questions.explanation: A passenger in the sidecar adds weight and changes how your motorcycle handles. Your motorcycle will need more distance to stop completely.

questions.question: Who is most likely to have a motorcycle crash?

options.text: Experienced riders.
Beginning riders.
Riders who know their motorcycle well.
Riders who completed a safety course.

questions.correctAnswerText: Beginning riders.
questions.explanation: Crashes happen most often to beginning riders who lack training and are not yet familiar with their motorcycle.

questions.question: When adjusting your mirrors, what should you see?

options.text: The road behind and to the sides of your motorcycle.
Your arms.
The road in front of your motorcycle.
The side of the motorcycle.

questions.correctAnswerText: The road behind and to the sides of your motorcycle.
questions.explanation: Adjust your mirrors to see the lane behind you and the lane next to you. You may see the edge of your arm or shoulder, but the road behind and to the side is most important.

questions.question: How can you tell your rear tire is flat while riding?

options.text: You hear a hissing sound from the back of the bike.
The back end jerks from side to side.
You cannot accelerate.
The rear brake stops working.

questions.correctAnswerText: The back end jerks from side to side.
questions.explanation: If your rear tire fails, the back of your motorcycle will jerk from side to side. You usually will not hear a tire fail.

questions.question: Passing other vehicles on a motorcycle is similar to passing in a car, except:

options.text: Being visible is more important on a motorcycle.
Being visible is less important on a motorcycle.
You should pass on the shoulder instead of the roadway.
You must make eye contact with the other driver.

questions.correctAnswerText: Being visible is more important on a motorcycle.
questions.explanation: Visibility is more critical on a motorcycle because motorcycles are smaller. Other drivers may not see you, or you may disappear into their blind spot.

questions.question: What should you do with a motorcycle helmet after it has been in a crash?

options.text: Inspect it carefully.
Replace it.
Sell it to another rider.
Install a new chinstrap.

questions.correctAnswerText: Replace it.
questions.explanation: Always replace any helmet that has been in a crash.

questions.question: When riding at night, you should:

options.text: Judge distances more easily than during the day.
Never use your high beam headlight because it makes it hard to see.
Stay in only one lane position.
Slow down.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down.
questions.explanation: At night, reduce your speed and increase your following distance. Use your high beam headlight when there is no other traffic. Adjust your lane position as needed for changing conditions.

questions.question: The center of a traffic lane has an oily strip from car drippings. This area is:

options.text: Never safe for motorcyclists.
Usually safe, unless the road is wet.
Usually safe, unless it is sunny.
Always safe, no matter the weather.

questions.correctAnswerText: Usually safe, unless the road is wet.
questions.explanation: Oily drippings collect in the center of traffic lanes. On dry roads, this area usually has enough grip for motorcycles. The oily strip is usually only two feet wide, so you can often ride around it while staying in the center of the lane.

questions.question: Successful motorcyclists know they are safest when other drivers can:

options.text: See them.
See them going faster than other vehicles.
See them on the side of the road.
See them on the left side of the lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: See them.
questions.explanation: Motorcyclists are safest when other drivers can see them clearly. Use your headlight, brake light, turn signals, and position yourself in the lane to be more visible.

questions.question: Which action does NOT help a rider become more visible?

options.text: Wearing bright clothing with reflective materials.
Using your headlight at all times.
Using your turn signals.
Waving at other drivers.

questions.correctAnswerText: Waving at other drivers.
questions.explanation: To be more visible, wear bright clothing with reflective materials, use your headlight at all times, and use your turn signals and brake light properly. Waving does not make you more visible.

questions.question: When preparing to pass another vehicle on the left, you should:

options.text: Ride on the right side of your lane.
Ride on the left side of your lane.
Get as close as possible to the vehicle in front of you.
Not signal your intentions.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ride on the left side of your lane.
questions.explanation: When passing on the left, ride on the left side of your lane. Signal your intentions and check for traffic. Pass when it is safe, then signal and return to your original lane.

questions.question: Why should a load be placed low on a motorcycle?

options.text: A high load raises the center of gravity.
A high load may block the turn signals.
A high load makes it hard to see over.
Other drivers cannot see a low load.

questions.correctAnswerText: A high load raises the center of gravity.
questions.explanation: A load placed too high will raise the motorcycle's center of gravity and make it harder to keep your balance.

questions.question: How can you be more visible at an intersection?

options.text: Try to make eye contact with other drivers.
Always ride with your headlight on.
Wave your arms.
Ride close to vehicles in front of you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Always ride with your headlight on.
questions.explanation: To be more visible at an intersection, always ride with your headlight on and position yourself where oncoming traffic can see you best. Keep enough space between you and other vehicles to react quickly if needed. Do not rely on eye contact alone.

questions.question: To stop quickly, you should:

options.text: Use only the front brake.
Use only the rear brake.
Use the front brake first, then the rear brake.
Use both brakes at the same time.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use both brakes at the same time.
questions.explanation: To stop quickly, apply both brakes at the same time.

questions.question: Approved helmets:

options.text: Can limit your view.
Let you see as far to the sides as you need.
Are dangerous to wear.
Do not have to be worn if they block your view.

questions.correctAnswerText: Let you see as far to the sides as you need.
questions.explanation: Some people worry that helmets limit vision, but this is not true. Approved helmets allow you to see as far to the sides as you need for safe riding.

questions.question: Making eye contact with other drivers:

options.text: Is the best way to know they see you.
Is not worth the effort.
Does not guarantee they will yield to you.
Guarantees they will yield to you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Does not guarantee they will yield to you.
questions.explanation: Never assume that eye contact with a driver means they will properly yield to you. Drivers often look directly at a motorcyclist but do not notice them.

questions.question: The gearshift lever is operated by:

options.text: Your right hand.
Your right foot.
Your left hand.
Your left foot.

questions.correctAnswerText: Your left foot.
questions.explanation: The gearshift lever is in front of the left footrest and is operated by your left foot.

questions.question: A major effect of drinking alcohol is:

options.text: Better riding abilities.
Slower body functions.
More nervousness.
More alertness.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slower body functions.
questions.explanation: Alcohol slows down your body functions. It weakens both your physical and mental abilities.
